test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 22 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Why do fats in diet form large globules in the small intestine?

options.text: Because fats do not mix well with watery slurry produced in the stomach
Because fats get trapped in fibrous carbohydrates during food churning in the stomach
Because proteins and fats clump together to produce colloidal matter
Because lipase enzymes in the stomach do not digest fats completely

solution:
The correct answer is __**option 1**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Because fats do not mix well with watery slurry produced in the stomach**:

 
 
• **Fats are hydrophobic (water-repelling) and do not mix easily with the water-based contents of the digestive tract.**
 
• In the stomach, partially digested food forms a watery mixture called chyme</em&g
